tickets.title: .MEAS does not give correct result in AC analysis
tickets.edits: Preserved original; replaced control AC/let/MEAS by equivalent .ac for dot-card measurement. Removed only post-processing control comparison, not .MEASURE par() or any devices.
tickets.expected: The two measurements perform different operations: post-processing abs(delta I)*delta Vdd is zero because the ideal DC supply has zero AC voltage. par() creates a nonlinear B-source f=abs(I)*Vdd whose AC Jacobian is delta f=Vdd_DC sign(I_DC) delta I+abs(I_DC) delta Vdd, generally nonzero; zero is not the correct expected B-source linearization.

ngspice47.evidence: zac_power0=-1.85801e+00; a nonzero B-source small-signal result is consistent with the derivative, not literal multiplication of AC phasors.

ngspiceMaster.evidence: not re-run on master: the defect does not reproduce on ngspice-47

spiceTs.evidence: UnsupportedMeasureError: par() needs B-source bpa_00 ... abs(i(vdd))*v(vdd); branch current i(...) references unsupported.

tickets.reproCheck: Mismatch is still visible as zac_power0=-1.85801, but par() AC linearization must not be confused with control post-processing yielding zero.
tickets.notes: Withdraw numeric-defect interpretation: original expected zero ignores DC-to-AC Jacobian semantics. No independently calculated BSIM4-specific coefficient; right verdict concerns operation semantics, not a high-precision value oracle.
